title: Bayesian Online Changepoint Detection
authors_or_org: Ryan Prescott Adams and David J. C. MacKay
supported_claim: Run-length posterior and predictive mixture under a product-partition model, conditional iid observations and a changepoint hazard.
limitations: Exact inference is model-conditional; no enterprise spend validation. Prior, hazard, likelihood and computational pruning affect behavior.
license_status: HTML identifies assumed arXiv perpetual non-exclusive license; no permissive code/data reuse license verified.

title: Learning from Time-Changing Data with Adaptive Windowing
published_or_version: Author extended manuscript dated 2006-10-17; shorter version SDM 2007, DOI 10.1137/1.9781611972771.42
supported_claim: Adaptive subwindow comparison; independent bounded input assumption; false-positive bound at each time step; ADWIN2 compression.
limitations: Not an organization-wide lifetime alarm bound; arbitrary dependent financial errors do not inherit its guarantee. Manuscript differs from conference version.
license_status: Author publications page says local preprints intended for personal noncommercial use and usual copyright restrictions apply; implementation license unverified.

title: 6.3.2.3.1. Cusum Average Run Length
published_or_version: Live handbook page; page revision date not verified
supported_claim: CUSUM reference value/decision threshold trade in-control average run length against detection delay; sensitivity depends on shift size.
limitations: Normality/standardization examples do not calibrate autocorrelated bursty spend streams or simultaneous monitoring of many teams.
license_status: Reuse terms not verified; government hosting alone not treated as a code/data license.

title: Regime-Switching Models
published_or_version: Author manuscript dated 2005-05-18, prepared for Palgrave Dictionary of Economics
supported_claim: Latent Markov states, filtered versus smoothed state probabilities, and difficulty estimating rich transitions from few observed regime changes.
limitations: Economic regime methods are not enterprise AI validation; state count and transition identifiability require care.
license_status: No explicit reusable code/data license verified in manuscript.

title: Selection of estimation window in the presence of breaks
authors_or_org: M. Hashem Pesaran and Allan Timmermann
supported_claim: Using some pre-break data can improve post-break forecasting through bias-variance tradeoffs; window cross-validation and combination are alternatives.
limitations: Fresh publisher-indexed abstract inspected; direct full publisher open returned 403. Results depend on regression assumptions and break size; not enterprise spend evidence.
license_status: Publisher rights link present; reuse license unverified.

title: Forecasting in the presence of recent structural change
authors_or_org: Jana Eklund, George Kapetanios and Simon Price; Bank of England
supported_claim: Compares monitored change, rolling regression, window averaging and EWMA; relative performance differs between stochastic and deterministic breaks.
limitations: Location-model analysis and macroeconomic experiments cannot establish ranking for this product's heterogeneous delayed targets.
license_status: Website copyright observed; reuse terms and code/data license not verified.

title: Dynamic Weighted Majority: An Ensemble Method for Drifting Concepts
authors_or_org: J. Zico Kolter and Marcus A. Maloof
supported_claim: Online ensemble weights, expert addition and removal respond to predictive performance.
limitations: Classification concept-drift evaluation; application to probabilistic regression and delayed cost targets is a proposed adaptation, not established performance.
license_status: Paper copyright names authors; reusable implementation/data license not verified.

title: Online Learning under Delayed Feedback
authors_or_org: Pooria Joulani, Andras Gyorgy and Csaba Szepesvari
supported_claim: Feedback delay changes online-learning regret; delay-aware reductions differ across adversarial and stochastic settings.
limitations: Theory does not provide a days-to-adaptation guarantee or direct calibration for billing revisions.
license_status: Paper copyright belongs to authors; specific code/data reuse license not verified.

title: A New Product Growth for Model Consumer Durables
published_or_version: Management Science 15(5):215-227, 1969-01-01; original published title preserved
supported_claim: Initial purchase timing modeled through innovation and imitation; original empirical application to eleven consumer durables.
limitations: Initial adoption is not repeated usage intensity, model substitution, centralized rollout, or AI token spending; no enterprise switch-speed conclusion.
license_status: Copyright 1969 INFORMS; no permissive reuse license verified.

title: Shifting Work Patterns with Generative AI
authors_or_org: Eleanor Wiske Dillon, Sonia Jaffe, Nicole Immorlica and Christopher T. Stanton
supported_claim: 66-firm workplace rollout distinguishes access from active use; use initially peaks and differs across firms, limiting a universal monotonic adoption assumption.
limitations: Selected knowledge workers and an integrated workplace assistant; no prompt content or token billing. Not a model of coding-agent adoption or rebound elasticity.
license_status: arXiv v4 license link verified as CC BY 4.0; underlying company telemetry reuse permission not established.

title: Claude API pricing
published_or_version: Live pricing documentation accessed 2026-10-24; no immutable version identifier verified
supported_claim: Model/token-category prices, cache operation distinctions, tool token overhead and additional server-tool billing can change effective cost independently of task counts.
limitations: Rates change and contracts/channels differ; documentation is not a customer's reported charge. Track intentionally does not freeze numerical prices.

title: Robust and Scalable Bayesian Online Changepoint Detection
authors_or_org: Matias Altamirano, Francois-Xavier Briol and Jeremias Knoblauch
supported_claim: Generalized Bayesian diffusion-score-matching change detection offers robustness and conjugate updates under specified conditions; ordinary BOCPD can mistake outliers for changes.
limitations: Robustness conditions and numerical examples do not establish enterprise-spend utility; rare large legitimate jobs still need exposure reporting.
license_status: Copyright 2023 authors observed in paper; reusable implementation/data license not verified.
